purpose: Test whether channel dropout costs EEGNet accuracy because the batch norms after the spatial filters store a training variance the test never sees, and whether dropout buys tolerance of a failed electrode.
claim_boundary: Exploratory for BCI IV 2a, planned after its test results and the overfitting-study results were known. For Lee2019 the predictions are fixed before any of the new models, and before any re-estimated or failed-electrode version of the archived models, is scored on Lee2019 session 2; the archived models' as-trained next-day scores were known. Three predictions, no correction for multiplicity.

B1.claim: Re-estimating the batch norms recovers next-day accuracy of the p = 0.2 models
B1.contrast: Lee2019 full-62-chdrop final models (scripts/overfit_study.py), next day: re-estimated minus as trained; also the share of the loss recovered, (re-estimated minus as trained) over (full-62 without dropout minus as trained)

B2.contrast: Lee2019 all-electrode final models, next day, as trained: p = 0.05 minus p = 0.2 (also reported with re-estimated batch norms)

B3.claim: A model trained with channel dropout loses less when one electrode fails
B3.contrast: Lee2019 all-electrode final models, next day, one electrode at its training mean, averaged over the 62: (intact minus failed) of full-62 without dropout as trained, minus the same of the dropout model with re-estimated batch norms, at the p of 0.05, 0.1, 0.2 with the best re-estimated held-out accuracy of the training day (fold models)

recalibration: mibci.noise_mechanism.recalibrate: the batch norms after the spatial filters (bnorm_1, bnorm_2) re-estimated in one cumulative pass over the training trials with every electrode present, dropout off
analysis: seeds (and folds) averaged within each participant; 95% participant bootstrap (10,000, seed 690); BCI IV 2a on artifact-free session-2 trials, Lee2019 on all; 2a also with the seed error
